title: AgentMail Launches AgentID to Let AI Agents Sign Into Apps
summary:
Authentication for AI agents now involves verified emails linked to human owners to prevent apps from blocking automated access. AgentMail released a system called AgentID that allows developers to identify the person behind each bot and set usage limits or disable specific agents as needed. Under this model, multiple agents belonging to one person are recognized as a single customer.

The integration is free for app developers and uses standard OpenID Connect to work with Clerk, Supabase, Auth0, Better Auth, and Auth.js. Early adopters including Firecrawl, Turso, Supermemory, and Keenable have already implemented the service. Startups that integrate the tool using a specific launch prompt and provide a screenshot receive 3 months of AgentMail plans at no charge.

selectedTweets.text:
AgentMail has launched AgentID, a sign-in option that allows AI agents to access apps with a verified email, similar to how 'Sign in with Google' works for people.

Each agent signs into apps with its own verified email, linked to a human owner. Apps that previously blocked agent signups can now allow them and see the owner behind each agent.

> 10 agents linked to one person appear as a single customer.

> Apps can set limits for each owner and disable individual agents.

> A human owner can be contacted if an issue occurs.
